newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stock market trade dominated by banks.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stock market trade dominated by banks.

text.p: Jordanian stocks was steady at end of weekly trade on Wednesday in dull activity dominated by a large bloc sale in Housing Bank, dealers said.
The Amman Financial Market 60-share index fell a slight 0.05 percent to 147.22 points from 147.31 points on Tuesday.
A total of 683,927 shares changed hands in high 1,563,821 dinars volume. Of 37 stock traded, five advanced, nineteen declined and 13 were unchanged.

Brokers said the market was buttressed by select trade on banking shares, with a large 200,000 share bloc sale -- alone accounting for nearly two thirds of total turnover -- in Housing Bank executed by institutional buyers.

Bank of Jordan was target of selling by some investors to a key bank shareholder seeking to increase his overall stake, dealers said. The stock was unchanged at 3.00 dinars. Amman Investment Bank was unchanged at 0.300 dinars in moderate 45,200 share turnover.
The market has remained in a wait-and-see mood since the recent flareup in violence in Palestinian self-rule areas.
Brokers say the market's plight has been worsened by lack of tangible progress in Israeli-Palestinian peace moves to give new impetus to the market, after a recent rebound lost steam.

After gradual gains end of last month that sent the market back above 150 points last week for the first time in four months, shares began to weaken after recent clashes flared in the Israeli occupied West Bank.
The market was hit this year by the breakdown of Middle East peace talks and the delay in implementing a limited oil-for-food deal with Jordan's biggest trading partner Iraq.
The private Pearl Investable Index of the 45 best performing shares on the exchange shed 0.09 percent to 80.98 points, still 15.21 percent down from the same time last year.
A total of 272,314 shares worth 140,016 dinars changed hands in weak trade in the parallel market. Of 14 shares traded, two advanced, seven declined and five were unchanged.
